scenes.text: Your AI assistant can read your email, check your calendar, even open your code. [1] So how does one AI connect to so many different apps? [2] The answer is MCP. Let's understand it.

Remember when every phone had its own charger? [1] AI tools had the same problem. Every app needed its own custom connection. [2] MCP is like USB-C for AI. One standard plug, so any AI can connect to any tool that supports it.

left.title: Before MCP
left.label: a new integration for every app

scenes.text: MCP stands for Model Context Protocol. [1] It's an open standard, first released by Anthropic, that lets AI apps connect to outside tools and data in one common way. So an AI can [2] use tools, [3] read your files and data, [4] and work with the apps you already use.

data.definition: An open standard that lets AI apps plug into outside tools and data in one common way.

scenes.text: Let's see how it flows. [1] You ask your AI app, what's on my calendar tomorrow? [2] Inside the app, an MCP client handles the connection. [3] It talks to an MCP server, a small program that knows how to work with your calendar. [4] The server fetches your events, [5] and the AI reads them and answers, you have two meetings tomorrow.

data.heading: How MCP works
nodes: Knows how to talk to the calendar

scenes.text: Four words to remember. [1] The host is the AI app you use, like Claude. [2] An MCP server is the connector for one app, like Gmail or GitHub. [3] Tools are the actions it offers, like sending an email. [4] And resources are the data it can share, like your documents.

data.heading: MCP in 4 words
terms: A connector for one app or data source

scenes.text: So where is MCP used today? [1] AI assistants that connect to your Gmail, Google Drive or Slack. [2] Coding assistants that read your project, and work with GitHub. [3] And companies that connect AI to their own internal databases, safely, through one standard.

Here's a common myth. [1] People think MCP only works with one company's AI. [2] It doesn't. It's an open standard, and many major AI companies and tools now support it. Build one MCP server, and lots of different AI apps can use it.

data.myth: MCP only works with one company's AI.
data.fact: It's an open standard. Build one MCP server, and many different AI apps can use it.

scenes.text: Let's recap. [1] MCP is like USB-C for AI. [2] Your AI app is the host, with an MCP client inside. [3] MCP servers connect it to apps and data. [4] And because it's open, you build once and connect everywhere. [5] Next, we'll see how AI can see, hear and speak, with multimodal AI. Follow AI Maastaaru!
